messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] kv-prefix coherency anomaly detected — 03:12 UTC. Spike in prefix miss + stale-read reports. Affected region: eu-west-1. Auto-escalation to oncall.
alice_g: I’m on it. seeing huge drop in kv_cache hit_ratio for prefix router. hitting backend more than usual. starting investigation.
raj_patel: oncall here. can you post the sample logs / metrics? curious if it’s an eviction storm or write-path invalidation.
alice_g: pasted latest metric snapshot:
```
prefix_cache.hit_ratio: 0.14 -> baseline 0.88
prefix_cache.evictions_per_min: 312 -> baseline 5
kv_write_retries: +7x
```
maria_k: noticed increased config-update churn from a tenant rollout earlier today (acme-inc). could be hot prefixes from that customer.
jordan_s: are we seeing correctness complaints or just latency/cost spike?
alice_g: both. a couple of customers reported stale completions (missing last-turn context) and we see retries/backpressure. customer-impact tag: partial correctness for ~2% requests in the last 20m.
oncall-sre: priority P1 until mitigations done. recommend traffic-shaping + selective cache bypass for suspect prefixes.
raj_patel: agree. plan proposal:
- step 1: apply soft rate-limit to background prefetch + maintenance jobs
- step 2: turn prefix caching to bypass for top-n hot prefixes from acme-inc (keep global cache on)
- step 3: temporarily increase eviction TTLs for other tenants to reduce churn
- step 4: monitor saturation and ramp down if tail latency increases
alice_g: starting step 1 now — throttling maintenance tasks (prefetch/compaction) to 10% of normal.
```
# command run
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/cacher -- /bin/sh -c "./maintenance_ctl --throttle=0.1"
```
ops-bot: maintenance tasks throttled: prefetch=0.1, compaction=0.1 (ack by infra)
alice_g: telemetry: evictions_per_min down to 185 after 45s. hit_ratio creeping to 0.22.
maria_k: preparing the selective bypass script for acme-inc prefixes. this will route requests matching the prefixes to origin (no prefix-level KV cache) while leaving global caches intact.
raj_patel: post the exact command before executing.
maria_k: command (dry-run shown):
```
./toggle_prefix_bypass --tenant=acme-inc --prefix-file=/tmp/acme_hot_prefixes.txt --mode=enable --reason="coherency-guard-1824"
```
jordan_s: how are we generating /tmp/acme_hot_prefixes.txt?
maria_k: using aggregation query against prefix-access logs: top 500 prefixes by QPS in last 10m.
```
SELECT prefix, count(*) as qps
FROM prefix_access
WHERE tenant = 'acme-inc' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
ORDER BY qps desc
LIMIT 500;
```
alice_g: ok go for it, but do in 50-prefix batches and watch error rate.
maria_k: enabling bypass batch 1 (50 prefixes).
ops-bot: toggle_prefix_bypass: batch=1/10, prefixes=50, action=enable, result=OK
alice_g: observing request latencies — small bump (~30ms) but error rate stable.
raj_patel: continue next batches until we hit threshold: if errors increase >1% absolute, stop and rollback.
maria_k: batch 2/10 applied.
maria_k: batch 3/10 applied.
alice_g: after batch 4, we see hit_ratio improved to 0.48 and evictions_per_min down to 42. customer reports of stale completions reduced.
oncall-sre: good. still need to cap per-tenant QPS for acme-inc to avoid rebuild storms when bypassing.
raj_patel: applying soft quota cut: reduce acme-inc burst quota by 30% across EU region for 20 minutes.
```
# command
./quota_ctl --tenant=acme-inc --region=eu-west-1 --set-burst=0.7 --duration=20m --reason="mitigation-coherency-1824"
```
ops-bot: quota change applied for acme-inc: burst=0.7, duration=20m
alice_g: telemetry now stable: latency and error rate within acceptable bounds. hit_ratio trending to 0.65.
jordan_s: any customers still impacted?
alice_g: one internal integration (acme-testing) still reporting sporadic truncated responses. digging log traces now.
maria_k: I traced a corner case: a race between prefix invalidation and long-running streaming responses. adding server-side guard to avoid serving cached prefix after an invalidate event.
raj_patel: is that a code deploy? if yes we should avoid for now — prefer config-level fixes.
maria_k: implemented guard via config flip (no code change): `prefix_serve_strict_invalidate=true` set on router config, safe to rollout.
```
# command
curl -X POST https://config-service.local/routers/eu-west-1/config -d '{"prefix_serve_strict_invalidate":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
ops-bot: config update accepted; rolling restart of 6 router pods scheduled.
alice_g: routers up with new config. traces show eliminated stale-serving paths for the traced sessions.
oncall-sre: summary so far: maintenance throttled, selective prefix bypass for acme hot prefixes done, acme burst quota reduced, router invalidation guard enabled. system stable. continuing to monitor.
jordan_s: handoff in 30min to next oncall. please produce quick incident summary and customer-impact notes in the ticket.
alice_g: creating incident ticket: INC-2026-1824 — prefix coherency mitigation, mitigation steps + timeline. tagging product + CS for customer comms.
maria_k: for postmortem: need to analyze why tenant rollout created hot prefixes (and consider rate-limiting control on config churn). also evaluate autoscaling thresholds for cache nodes.
raj_patel: agreed. next actions after handoff: revert temporary quota/bypass after 2h if stable, and run a canary for config churn protection.
oncall-sre: leaving the thread to next oncall @jordan_s. add me if anything breaks. :white_check_mark:
jordan_s: taking handoff. will watch metrics and validate rollback plan at +1h.
incident-bot: Auto-note: page acknowledged by alice_g. elapsed time to mitigation (soft): 18 minutes. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
